description: One page whose single FlateDecode content stream inflates to 12 MiB.
proves: A single stream cannot inflate past the decompression ceiling, and the refusal is a named, actionable finding rather than "unparseable".
name: single-stream-bomb

description: 16 FlateDecode content streams of 1 MiB each: 16 MiB decoded in total, no single stream anywhere near a per-stream ceiling.
proves: The budget is aggregate. A per-stream ceiling alone accepts this document and retains 16 MiB for it; the running total is what refuses it.
name: many-small-streams-bomb

description: An indirect object holding 400 levels of directly nested arrays.
proves: Nesting fails closed inside the parser (256-level ceiling) instead of recursing until the stack or the memory limit decides.
name: deep-nesting-bomb

description: A cross-reference stream whose /Index declares 5,000,000 entries from 20 bytes of dictionary.
proves: The object ceiling is consulted while the cross-reference data is read, before the entries it declares are built.
name: object-count-bomb

description: 40 pages of ordinary contract prose across 40 FlateDecode content streams.
proves: The ceilings admit a document that is genuinely large. If this one is refused, the budget is set wrong rather than the document being hostile.
name: large-legitimate-control

description: One page whose CTM is multiplied past the double range before text is shown.
proves: Preflight bounds the document, not the arithmetic inside it. Text extraction is where an impossible transform is caught, and it has to leave as an unreadable document rather than as an uncaught geometry error.
name: overflowing-transform

description: One page whose content stream shows a single one-megabyte string with one Tj.
proves: One text-showing operator is not one unit of work. Its glyphs are decoded under the document's budget as they are read, not after the whole string has been expanded.
name: long-shown-string

description: One page whose content stream is half a million numbers and no operator.
proves: A stream that yields no operation still costs its tokens. The tokenizer charges them itself, because a walk that charges per operation is never called.
name: operand-flood

description: One page shown in a font whose /ToUnicode CMap is a megabyte of bfchar entries.
proves: A font's /ToUnicode map is lexed by the same tokenizer as a page, and is charged to the same document: the page walk charges nothing while the fonts it needs are being read.
name: cmap-flood
